root_idea.summary: The root conveys two related orientations: something not reckoned with or significant, and habitual absorption in or repetition of something, especially speech.
root_idea.development: These orientations yield terms for vain or unprofitable speech, speech uttered without deliberate intent, repeated or habitual utterance, and language as speech habitually used by a group. Quranic usage centers on idle or objectionable speech and its avoidance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form لَغَا rather than the Quranic plural imperative.
Displayed as the normalized masculine active-participle citation form لَاغٍ; the Quran occurrence is its feminine form لَاغِيَةً.
Displayed under the standard noun لَغْو.

senses.definition: To speak idly or make distracting, unprofitable noise.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is a plural imperative in a context of obstructing attentive listening; it belongs to the speech/noise branch of the root.

senses.definition: Vain or idle speech; speech of no account.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the feminine form لَاغِيَةً is used adjectivally of speech that is heard; it is an active-participial expression for لَغْو.

senses.definition: Speech or utterance of no account: idle, vain, unprofitable, or objectionable talk.
senses.usage_conditions: It may describe speech produced without deliberation or thought. In Quranic avoidance constructions, it refers either to such speech or to encountering people engaged in it, without requiring a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: An oath uttered without deliberate inward resolve to contract a binding oath.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction لَغْوٌ فِي الأَيْمَان concerns habitual or mistaken oath-language that was not intentionally affirmed as an oath; it is distinct from a deliberately contracted oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something not reckoned with, of no account, or unprofitable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic application beyond the Quranic speech usages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Young camels not counted in a blood-money assessment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported specialized usage in the terminology of blood-money compensation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chirping or vocal sound of sparrows and similar birds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bird-call sense provides the comparison for habitual or repeated utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be absorbed in or habitually occupied with a matter; to keep repeating or dwelling on it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with بِ; the usage describes habitual attachment to a subject or utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To jest or joke with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III verb, with the person involved as the participant in the joking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The genuine or classical language of the Arabs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the established language itself, not merely an isolated utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to the genuine or classical Arabic language; lexicological or linguistic in meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival derivative used of language-related matters or meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A word or linguistic report of weak authority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A depreciative classical usage concerning the reliability or authority of a word.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form III joking usage is represented.
Covers no-account speech and the broader no-account/unprofitable application.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the oath expression.
Language-related adjective and lexicological usage are represented.

cautions: The Quranic verb is a plural imperative and is normalized to the Form I citation form لَغَا.
The Quranic لَاغِيَةً is a feminine active participle used of speech; the public headword is normalized to لَاغٍ.
The oath sense concerns unintentional or non-deliberately contracted oath-language, not deliberate false or binding oaths.

The discussion of the Quranic avoidance passage in 25:72 preserves two contextual explanations: avoiding explicit ugly speech and declining to engage with its speakers. These remain applications of the same vain/objectionable-speech sense.
